chunks: And that which was narrated is: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad from Abdillah ibn al-Mughira from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"There is no harm in the fasting person undergoing cupping, except in Ramadan, for I dislike that he endanger himself, unless he fears for his life. And indeed, when we intend, if we seek cupping in Ramadan, we perform it at night."

So it is not contradictory to what we mentioned, because he only disliked cupping in Ramadan - and attached it to the state of necessity when the person fears weakness. As for one who does not fear weakness, then there is no harm in it in any case.
ai.seo_question: Is cupping permissible for a fasting person during Ramadan?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) to clarify the juristic nuance between general permissibility and the specific dislike (karahah) of cupping during Ramadan due to potential weakening of the fast. The text highlights the principle of 'la gharar' (avoiding self-endangerment), noting that the Imam himself practiced cupping at night in Ramadan to mitigate this risk, thereby establishing a practical precedent for necessity versus precaution.
